patch_description: The single-point random search plateaus because moving one point while all others are fixed rarely lifts the true bottleneck: the minimal triangles typically share several points, so a coordinated "group move" is needed. I add (a) two more deterministic seeds (concentric-rings layout and Dirichlet sample), and (b) a group-move annealing phase where 2-4 points are perturbed jointly in the hard-min phase — the mechanism that reportedly drove the best-known generation to 0.80. To keep runtime near the ~8.4s budget, I trim the single-point hard phase iterations and vectorize the trial evaluation via a cheaper incremental min-area check (recompute only areas involving moved points, using the cached full area matrix of ordered triples). Concretely: precompute index arrays for triples; when a subset S of points moves, only triplets containing indices in S change. Since random trials only move 2-4 points, this cuts the O(C(11,3))=165 evaluations per iteration to typically 100+, but the copy overhead is avoided by mutating and undoing, and using np.ix_ on a precomputed triple index matrix. Net effect: group moves unlock better min areas while staying within budget.
